content_of_post_to_answer: How does accepting your own flaws as a "bad example" actually make it easier for you to improve yourself?
answer: Accepting yourself as a “bad example” works because it removes the need to defend the version of yourself that is causing problems. Once you stop protecting your ego, your mistakes become data instead of threats. I’ve explored this pattern in more detail on my profile for anyone interested in how self-awareness changes behavior. The paradox is that people improve faster when they stop trying to prove they are already good.
